Download a friction surface at the resolution of the analysis

Source: R/friction.R
friction.Rd

friction() retrieves a friction surface layer from the Malaria Atlas Project (MAP) database (Hay et al., 2006; Weiss et al., 2018, 2020) and produces it at the spatial resolution of the analysis, following the rules used to build the MAP surfaces.

Friction values are expressed in minutes required to travel one meter.

An internet connection is required, unless the data are supplied via file and roads, or were cached by a previous call with cache = TRUE.

Usage

friction(
  bb_area,
  mode = "walk",
  dowscaling_model_type = NULL,
  res_output = 100,
  cache = FALSE,
  file = NULL,
  roads = NULL,
  road_speeds = default_road_speeds()
)

Arguments

bb_area

A sf object with the polygon(s) of the area of interest.

mode

(optional) A character string indicating the mode of transport. Options are "fastest" and "walk" (default: "walk").

  • For "fastest": The friction layer accounts for multiple modes of transport, including walking and driving. At the native resolution, it is the Malaria Atlas Project (2015) Global Travel Speed Friction Surface.

  • For "walk": The friction layer accounts only for walking speeds and is based on the Malaria Atlas Project (2020) Global Walking Only Friction Surface.

dowscaling_model_type

Deprecated and ignored. The friction surface is no longer downscaled with a statistical model (see Details).

res_output

(optional) A positive integerish number indicating the spatial resolution of the friction raster (and of the analysis), in meters. See Details (default: 100).

cache

(optional) A logical flag indicating whether to cache downloaded data (friction surface of the area, road network) on disk and reuse it in later calls. It also enables a fallback to a one-time download of the global friction surface (~730 MB) when the Malaria Atlas Project service is unavailable. See Details of friction() (default: FALSE).

file

(optional) A character string indicating the path to a local Malaria Atlas Project friction surface raster file, used instead of downloading it: the walking-only surface, except with mode = "fastest" and res_output >= 1000, where it is the travel speed surface (default: NULL).

roads

(optional) A sf object with the road network (LINESTRING or MULTILINESTRING geometries), used when mode = "fastest" and res_output < 1000. It must have either a speed column with speeds in km/h, or a highway column with OpenStreetMap road classes, which are converted to speeds with road_speeds. If NULL, the road network is downloaded from OpenStreetMap (default: NULL).

road_speeds

(optional) A named numeric vector with the speed (km/h) of each OpenStreetMap road class (highway tag). Road classes not in road_speeds are ignored (default: default_road_speeds()).

Value

An invisible list with the following elements:

  • friction_layer: A RasterLayer object with the friction surface layer (minutes per meter).

  • transition_matrix: A TransitionLayer with the transition matrix for cost-distance calculations.

  • geocorrection_matrix: A TransitionLayer with the geocorrection matrix for accurate distance calculations.

Details

Spatial resolution

The MAP surfaces have a resolution of 30 arc-seconds (~1 km). When res_output >= 1000, the surface of the chosen mode is used at its native resolution.

When res_output < 1000, the surface is produced on a grid of about res_output meters following the rule used to build the MAP surfaces: within each cell, the fastest mode of transport takes precedence (Weiss et al., 2018).

  • mode = "walk": MAP assigns the same walking speed (5 km/h) to roads and to urban land, so the road network adds no information at a finer resolution. The walking-only surface is resampled to the finer grid (nearest neighbor) without changing its values.

  • mode = "fastest": cells crossed by a road get the speed of the fastest road crossing them (see road_speeds). All other cells get the friction of the MAP walking-only surface, which accounts for land cover and slope. Railways, ferries and congestion are not modeled.

The road network is downloaded from OpenStreetMap (OSM) through the Overpass API, unless it is supplied via roads.

Online data and fallbacks

Online services can be unavailable or overloaded. The friction surface is obtained from the first available of these sources:

  1. With cache = TRUE, the surface of the area cached by a previous call, or a cached copy of the global surface.

  2. The MAP data service (retried once).

  3. With cache = TRUE, a one-time download of the global surface (~730 MB) from a mirror on the Open Science Framework (OSF), which is then cached.

If none is available, the error message suggests downloading the global surface manually and supplying it via file.

The road network is obtained from the cache (with cache = TRUE) or from several public Overpass API servers in turn (each with a single attempt of at most ~2.5 minutes), skipping those that are unreachable or at capacity. If none responds, a warning is issued and the MAP travel speed surface (~1 km) is used on the finer grid instead.

Cached data are stored in tools::R_user_dir("locationallocation", "cache"). The following options change the default behavior:

  • locationallocation.cache_dir: the cache directory.

  • locationallocation.overpass_urls: the Overpass API servers to try, in order.

  • locationallocation.retry_wait: the number of seconds to wait before retrying a failed download (default: 30).
